title: Endotracheal tube care

sources.use: 2024 AARC patient-ventilator assessment CPG (cite only; permission needed to reproduce)

objectives: Check and record tube position and securement.
Explain how cuff pressure is measured and why palpation is unreliable.
Describe measures that reduce ventilator-associated complications.
Escalate suspected displacement or obstruction immediately.

items.text: Care applies to every patient with an endotracheal tube in place.
Measure cuff pressure with a manometer; palpating the pilot balloon is inaccurate (AARC strong recommendation, high certainty).

Do not use continuous cuff-pressure monitoring as a VAP-prevention measure (AARC strong recommendation against; SHEA does not recommend automated or frequent monitoring for VAP prevention). Neither document says intermittent checks should stop.
Keep the head of the bed raised unless contraindicated, and give mouth care with toothbrushing and no chlorhexidine (SHEA essential practices).
Check and document tube depth marking and securement as often as policy requires and after every move, turn, transfer or procedure; assess skin around the airway device.
Prevent unplanned extubation: assess agitation, optimise analgesia and sedation per protocol, avoid circuit traction.
Who re-secures the tube, measures cuff pressure and changes the tube holder varies by country and unit; follow local policy.
Manometer, tube holder and securement products follow unit supplies.
An appropriate cuff pressure range of 20-30 cmH2O appears in AARC narrative text (not a graded recommendation); there is no consensus on how often to measure. Use the unit target.
Re-securing technique, depth checks and cuff adjustment follow the unit's approved procedure; no source read describes the steps.
Tube depth and securement, cuff pressure at policy intervals, SpO2, end-tidal CO2 and waveform, expired tidal volume and airway pressures, secretions, skin and mouth, sedation and agitation.

Escalate immediately for suspected displacement or obstruction, loss of capnography trace, severe desaturation, uncorrectable cuff failure, accidental extubation or new airway bleeding, and call for help.

Accidental extubation, endobronchial intubation, obstruction, aspiration around the cuff, tracheal injury from over-inflation, pressure injury of lips, mouth, nose or face, ventilator-associated pneumonia.
Record tube size and depth, securement, cuff pressure and time, skin and mouth findings, capnography confirmation, events and escalation per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Confirm the tube depth marking matches the recorded depth and the tube is secure.
Confirm a capnography trace and ventilator waveform are present.
Measure cuff pressure with a manometer at the unit interval; do not judge it by feeling the pilot balloon.
Check skin and mouth around the tube and securement.
Keep the head of the bed raised unless contraindicated.
Call for help at once for suspected displacement, obstruction or loss of the capnography trace.
Record depth, securement, cuff pressure and time.

gaps: Cuff target range and interval: unit decision; AARC range is narrative, not graded.
Securement method, restraint policy, who re-secures: unsourced.
Extubation criteria and cuff-leak tests: out of scope of sources read.
